text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to $131.83, continuing a sharp two-week decline that's largely reflected in the underlying oil market. The trigger: on September 17th, oil prices dropped after Saudi Arabia signaled it would boost crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz following a pipeline attack, easing supply concerns that had been supporting prices. That relief trade has persisted, with crude finishing the week essentially flat despite Middle East tensions, which means the immediate supply-shock premium has evaporated.

The broader backdrop is a shift in how the market is pricing geopolitical risk. A week ago, concerns about widening Saudi-Houthi conflict and U.S. military action in Iran pushed oil higher; now, signs of potential de-escalation (Trump saying the U.S. may be nearing an end to its Iran war) and Saudi assurances of steady supply have flipped that dynamic. For an integrated oil company like this one, lower oil prices directly compress margins and earnings power, which is why the stock has slid alongside crude.
